abstract.p: We present a robust framework for deploying domain-specific language agents that can query industrial sensor data using natural language. Grounded in the Reasoning and Acting (Re-Act) paradigm, our system introduces three key innovations: (1) integration of the Self-Ask method for compositional, multi-hop reasoning; (2) a multi-agent architecture with Review, Reflect and Distillation components to improve reliability and fault tolerance; and (3) a long-context prompting strategy leveraging curated in-context examples, which we call Tiny Trajectory Store, eliminating the need for fine-tuning. We apply our method to Industry 4.0 scenarios, where agents query SCADA systems (e.g., SkySpark) using questions such as, "How much power did B002 AHU 2-1-1 use on 6/14/16 at the POKMAIN site?" To enable systematic evaluation, we introduce IoTBench, a benchmark of 400+ tasks across five industrial sites. Our experiments show that ReAct-style agents enhanced with long-context reasoning (ReActXen) significantly outperform standard prompting baselines across multiple LLMs, including smaller models. This work repositions NLP agents as practical interfaces for industrial automation. The code/data can be found here.
